# Judges Chapter 17 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), c. 1008 CE | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JDG_page_287.jpg

### Micah's Idols

1. There was a man named Micah, who lived in the hill country of Ephraim.

2. One day he said to his mother, "I heard you utter a curse about the 1,100 pieces of silver that were stolen from you. Well, I have the money. I was the one who took it." "The LORD bless you, my son!" his mother said.

3. He returned the silver to his mother, and she said, "I now dedicate this silver to the LORD. My son, I am giving it to you to have an image carved and an idol cast." So he gave it back to her.

4. She took 200 pieces of silver to a silversmith, who made them into a carved image and a cast idol. And it was placed in Micah's house.

5. This man Micah had his own shrine. He made an ephod and some household idols, and he installed one of his sons as his personal priest.

6. In those days Israel had no king; everyone did as they saw fit.

7. Now a young Levite had been living in Bethlehem in Judah.

8. He left Bethlehem to find another place to stay. As he traveled, he came to Micah's house in the hill country of Ephraim.

9. "Where are you from?" Micah asked him. "I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah," he replied, "and I am looking for a place to live."

10. "Stay here with me," Micah said, "and be my father and priest. I'll give you ten pieces of silver a year, plus a new set of clothes and your food." So the Levite agreed,

11. and he was content to live with Micah. He became like one of Micah's sons.

12. Micah installed the Levite as his personal priest, and the young man lived in his house.

13. "Now I know the LORD will bless me," Micah said, "because I have a Levite serving as my priest!"

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**The parody of religion:** Everything in this chapter is a parody of legitimate Israelite worship. Micah steals silver from his own mother (v.2). She "dedicates" it to the LORD — then uses it to make an idol (v.3). Of 1,100 pieces, only 200 go to the silversmith — even the dedication is half-hearted (v.4). Micah builds his own shrine, makes his own ephod, and ordains his own priest — first his son, then a wandering Levite (vv.5, 12). He thinks he's secured God's blessing (v.13), but every element of his worship violates the Torah.

**"Everyone did as they saw fit" (v.6):** This is the key to the entire final section of Judges (chapters 17-21). Without a king — meaning without a central authority enforcing covenant faithfulness — religion becomes a self-serving consumer product. You pick your gods, hire your priest, and assume you're blessed.

— PNEUMA, AI Translator
